correctness.rationale: For any DIM, black matched vertices have exactly one black neighbor while white vertices have none. On GP(n,2) the outer-white gaps have lengths two or three, and each white outer vertex forces exactly one adjacent gap to have length two, thus alternation of two/three and n divisible by five. Outer states uniquely determine inner states and matching edges. The five rotations of an explicit period-five template exist, are distinct, and partition all 3n edges. A cubic graph maximal matching has >=3n/5 edges, and equality forces disjoint five-edge closed neighborhoods, hence a DIM. Every strong five-coloring has each of the five colors exactly once in each closed edge neighborhood, hence classes are exactly the five DIMs. Independent exact-cover enumeration n=5..30 and separate vertex-state enumeration n=5..20 agree with proof. Finite enumeration not used for infinite inference.

value.rationale: The graph GP(n,2) is a canonical cubic family; the 2024 literature establishes a natural periodic DIM but does not classify all efficient edge dominators. The new gap alternation theorem proves structural rigidity of every optimum, exhausts five globally incompatible solutions, and yields a unique optimum strong edge-color partition and all equality-case minimum maximal matchings across infinitely many orders. This is a mathematically motivated classification, not an arbitrary finite count or routine parameter substitution.
